title: GUARD (fixed in 96382cfb71) — was: `cd \`<newline>`/usr/sh`: zsh completes /usr/share/, zshrs leaves the word and prints two _describe errors

observed.detail: diverges at step #1 ('tab'); first diff row 1 col 7; 4 row(s) differ
observed.notes: Both shells answer the Enter with PS2 — the buffer is deliberately incomplete at the newline, so nothing executes and the completion fires inside the continuation. The single-line control below completes the same word with the newline removed and PASSES, which is what makes the CONTINUATION the variable rather than the word. One zstyle statement is enough: `list-grouped false`. zshrs emits `_describe:compdescribe:122: invalid argument: __galiases_ary` and `_describe:compdescribe:129: no parsed state` before drawing the same completion one row lower, so the line the user sees is still `/usr/sh` where zsh has already inserted `/usr/share/`.

controls.note: `cd /usr/sh` on one line under the same single zstyle: PASSES.

confirmed.note: RETIRED AS A GUARD. `expect` flipped diverges -> agrees on this run: scripts/compsys_regressions.py scored the cell NOW-PASSES three attempts running and its control CONTROL-HOLDS. Attributed, not assumed — the SAME runner, same fixtures, same session, against a pinned build of the parent commit (sha256 6c6f9493cd9a958c) still scored this cell STILL-DIVERGES, 4 row(s) differ from step #1 (tab). The cause is 96382cfb71, which ports docomplete's chline prepend (zle_tricky.c:640-653) and the c:681-690 decline it carries, so completion on a PS2 continuation lexes the lines already entered instead of the physical line alone.
